data.title: ComEd, League of Chicago Theatres Award $205,000 in Grants to Support the Arts
data.description:
ComEd and the League of Chicago Theatres today announced the recipients of the 2026 Powering the Arts Grant Program. Celebrating its ninth year, the program is awarding a total of $205,000 to 19 nonprofit organizations across northern Illinois. These funds will support a range of arts initiatives, from youth creative development to engaging community experiences.

“ComEd is proud to partner with the League of Chicago Theatres to support local arts programs that enrich our neighborhoods,” said Melissa Washington, senior vice president of Government, Regulatory and External Affairs at ComEd. “This year’s recipients continue to advance that mission. Each project celebrates the vibrancy of our communities, and they collectively expand access to live performances, music education, community festivals and opportunities for creative expression for the people we serve.”

Since its launch in 2018, the Powering the Arts Grant Program has awarded nearly $1.5 million in grant funding to support over 150 different arts and cultural projects within the ComEd service territory. ComEd and the League of Chicago Theatres work closely together to administer the program. Grant applications are reviewed by an external panel of judges, and grant recipients match the award funding with their own investment of equal or greater value towards their project.

“Arts and culture enrich our neighborhoods and play an essential role in building thriving communities,” said Executive Director of the Chicago League of Theatres Marissa Lynn Jones. “As we enter the 2027 grant season, our ongoing partnership with ComEd reflects a shared commitment to strengthening the arts sector and expanding access to creative experiences across our region. By supporting local arts organizations, we are helping them deepen their community impact, engage new audiences, and contribute to more vibrant, connected, and resilient communities.”

ComEd remains committed to working with local organizations to invest in projects that improve quality of life for northern Illinois residents. The Powering the Arts Grant Program is one of ComEd’s four Power for Good grant programs empowering communities across northern Illinois together with the Powering Safe Communities Grant Program, the Green Region Grant Program and the Powering the Holidays Grant Program.

More information about ComEd grant opportunities is available at ComEd.com/Grants.

The 2026 ComEd Powering the Arts Grant Program recipients and their funded projects include:

Paramount Arts Centre, Inc (Aurora) will expand its programming that creates meaningful opportunities to experience live theater with more targeted theater engagement events serving more than 500 Aurora educators, nurses, first responders, veterans and seniors.

Mandi Theater (Buffalo Grove) will expand its accessibility initiative throughout its 10th Annual International Theatre Festival by removing financial, linguistic, and engagement barriers.

John Walt Foundation (Chicago, Austin) will expand its six-week Summer Apprenticeship Program, providing 20 to 25 West Side youth with paid creative arts and workforce development opportunities.

The Chicago Mosaic School (Chicago, Edgewater) will relaunch its Teaching the Teachers program, providing affordable mosaic arts training to approximately 200 local educators who collectively serve more than 3,000 students.

The World Music Foundation (Chicago, Edgewater) will present 22 live world music sessions for approximately 660 seniors and families, bringing global music experiences directly to those living in Chicago affordable housing communities.

UrbanTheater Company (Chicago, Humboldt Park) will launch Cruzando Generaciones (Crossing Generations), a weekend theater workshop series for Humboldt Park and surrounding area high school students that connects teens and older adults through theater, storytelling and oral history.

Uniting Voices (Chicago, Hyde Park) will expand upon and launch new North Lawndale school programs to provide choral instruction and performance opportunities impacting up to 300 students.

Culture Shock Chicago NFP (Chicago, Lincoln Park) will expand its Shockwaves hip-hop arts program to rural northern Illinois schools and communities who currently have limited arts access, reaching approximately 3,000 students and community members.

Young People's Theatre of Chicago (Chicago, Lincoln Park) will launch the Student Access Initiative aimed at expanding access to live theater for approximately 1,500 students from 25 Chicago Public Schools through free tickets and transportation assistance.

Midnight Circus in the Parks (Chicago, Lincoln Square) will bring four free circus performances, interactive juggling activities and dedicated transportation from a local senior center to Brighton Park, providing access for up to 1,600 attendees.

Villapalooza Inc. (Chicago, Little Village) will expand its free Little Village Arts and Music Festival that includes local and national artists, community resources and ongoing public engagement, reaching more than 3,000 attendees.

The Joffrey Ballet (Chicago, Loop) will present Joffrey for All, a free outdoor dance performance at Gallagher Way expected to reach up to 3,000 people.

Project H.O.O.D. (Chicago, South Side) will launch its first dedicated theater and performing arts program which will provide 40 to 60 children in Englewood and Woodlawn with free theater training before a public community showcase.

TimeLine Theatre Company (Chicago, Uptown) will provide Chicago teens with a free six-week summer program combining theater training, professional mentorship and a paid opportunity to create original performances.

Illinois Conservatory for the Arts (DuPage) will launch the IMPACT Access Initiative to provide free or low-cost performing arts opportunities to approximately 250 students and create pathways into scholarships, return events and audition preparation.

Elgin Youth Symphony Orchestra, Inc. (Elgin) will provide free after-school violin and viola instruction and instruments to fourth-grade students across the Fox Valley region.

Angels Athletics (Flossmoor) will expand its Angels in the Arts programming through artist workshops, cultural outings, dance and an intergenerational musical production serving youth, families and seniors.

Freeport Art Museum (Freeport) will expand Paint the Port to include more live music and additional sponsored painting opportunities for approximately 1,500 participants and visitors.

Spotlight Performance Academy (Homewood) will launch a new senior community choir in Homewood and Flossmoor, engaging at least 60 seniors in music and intergenerational performances.

ComEd is a unit of Chicago-based Exelon Corporation (NASDAQ: EXC), a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving more than 10.7 million electricity and natural gas customers. ComEd powers the lives of more than 4.2 million customers across northern Illinois, or 70 percent of the state’s population. For more information, visit ComEd.com, and connect with the company on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X and YouTube.

data.title: AP sues to challenge limits on access to US lawsuits by immigration detainees
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

The Associated Press sued the U.S. federal judiciary on Tuesday to challenge the constitutionality of a rule that has restricted reporters' ability to easily access lawsuits by people detained as part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

The news service in a lawsuit filed in a federal court in Washington, D.C., said thousands of people arrested during Trump's efforts to ramp up deportations have filed cases alleging they ​were unlawfully detained.

Like other media outlets, the AP said that it has sought to report on the so-called habeas cases "due to the immense public interest in the federal government’s immigration enforcement policies and the treatment of detainees in its custody."

"But over and over, AP reporters have met a roadblock that substantially impedes AP’s ability to report on these immigration habeas cases in a timely fashion, and in some respects prevents covering these cases at all," the lawsuit said.

The lawsuit challenges a provision of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure that restricts remote electronic access to documents filed in immigration-related cases, preventing them from being downloaded from the online court records system known as the Public Access to Court Electronic Records, or PACER.

While such records are public, they can only be accessed usually by going to the courthouse where they are filed and requesting access in person through a clerk's office, where they can often be viewed on a public terminal.

The AP argues that under the U.S. Constitution's First Amendment, those records are subject to a qualified right of access and should be available via PACER like other court documents.

It said the rule also constitutes an unconstitutional content-based restriction because it restricts access to filings based solely on a case's subject matter, in this case immigration.

"The result — even if unintentional — is that immigrants’ claims of unlawful detention by the federal government are much less visible to the public than other kinds of federal lawsuits," the lawsuit contends.

The lawsuit names as a defendant the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, the judiciary's administrative arm. A spokesperson for the Administrative Office declined to comment.

The lawsuit was filed by lawyers at the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, which in May separately asked the U.S. Judicial Conference's Committee on Rules of Practice and Procedure to revise the rule to remove the restrictions on electronic access to the immigration-related records.

The proposed rule change has been referred to a Judicial Conference advisory committee, which next meets on October 21. Any change, though, would likely take years to wind through the judiciary's usual rulemaking process.

The case is The Associated Press v. Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, No. 1:26-cv-03219.

For the AP: Renee Griffin and Adam Marshall of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press

data.description:

Loss from operations was $2.9 million, and the company recorded a $0.3 million inventory reserve related to its wavECG device. As of July 31, 2026, HeartSciences had a shareholders’ deficit of $2.0 million and has since raised additional capital through equity sales and ATM offerings.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: No meaningful revenue reported for FQ1 2027.
  • Loss from operations: $2.9 million for FQ1 2027 (FQ1 2026: $1.9 million).
  • Net loss: $3.2 million for FQ1 2027 (FQ1 2026: $2.1 million).
  • Inventory reserve: $0.3 million reserve recorded against wavECG-related inventory.
  • Shareholders’ deficit: $2.0 million as of July 31, 2026; subsequent financings raised approximately $1.0 million from Fortitude and approximately $1.2 million net from ATM sales.

Business Highlights

  • Proposed transaction: Continued progress toward a business combination with Fortitude, expected to close in Q4 calendar 2026 subject to customary conditions and shareholder approval.
  • MyoVista Insights commercial traction: First U.S. commercial agreements signed following full launch and selection as the AI-ECG delivery platform for a clinical program at a major European reference center with potential to expand to a multicenter project.
  • Platform upgrades and marketplace: MyoVista Insights reached version 1.4 and added the first third-party FDA-cleared AI-ECG algorithm to its marketplace, enabling cloud-based delivery of AI algorithms into clinical workflows.

  • wavECG device status: FDA 510(k) submission remains under review; company does not plan significant additional investment in device commercialization given regulatory, R&D, and commercial considerations and the shift toward cloud-based AI-ECG delivery.

data.title: U.S. Dollar Inches Higher Amid Increasing Fed Rate Hike Bets As Crude Oil Prices Surge
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Dollar value ticked higher on Tuesday as traders raised their bets on interest rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve at the end of its two-day meeting tomorrow following fresh crude oil supply disruption concerns after Saudi Arabia announced closure of its vital pipeline.

Today, the U.S. Dollar Index DXY, which measures the Greenback against a basket of other major currencies, was last seen trading at 99.64, up by 0.16 (or 0.16%).

While against the Euro, the USD was trading at 1.154, up by 0.06%, against the GBP, the USD was trading at 1.347, up by 0.18%.

Against the USD, the Japanese Yen was trading at 155.118, down by 0.50%, the Swiss Franc was trading at 0.819, down by 0.18%; and the Canadian Dollar was trading at 1.392, down by 0.15%.

Against one unit of Australian Dollar, the USD was trading at 0.713, up by 0.11%.

In the Middle East, after Saudi Arabia shut its vital East-West pipeline last Friday, fresh concerns of oil and energy supply disruption have emerged, reinforcing inflationary concerns.

Suffering a series of drone attacks on its 1,200-km-long East-West Pipeline by Iran-linked Houthi militant group of Yemen, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy confirmed temporarily closing the line to begin repair works.

Serving as an alternative channel for oil exports, it allowed Saudi Arabia to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The extent of damage is not fully known. Saudi Arabia is yet to disclose a timetable for the completion of repair works though experts view that it could take several weeks.

With nearly around 4 million barrels per day of crude oil export at risk, energy traders have priced in supply disruption possibilities for an extended time.

Adding to concerns, Houthis captured the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

The advance of Houthi militants across Yemen's Red Sea coast could potentially offer Iran a leverage to control oil and energy movement in the Arab region.

A planned meeting between the member countries of the Gulf Cooperation Council and Iran, slated to be held in Oman on Monday, was cancelled without any announcement on a future date.

U.S. President Donald Trump announced through Truth Social that Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly, and added that the U.S. was open to dialogues.

Dismissing Trump's claims, the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei announced that there would not be any talks until Iran's conditions are met.

Another claim by Trump yesterday that Russia and Ukraine agreed to halt their attacks on each other's energy installations was refuted by Ukraine. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy affirmed that Ukraine will halt its attacks but only if Russia too stops its attacks.

In Libya, the National Oil Corporation threatened to declare force majeure after security force members (Petroleum Facilities Guard) assigned to protect the country's oil infrastructure shut a pipeline valve and halted production at Hamada and Tahara oil fields.

With production and supply-linked concerns, crude oil traded above the $105-per-barrel range after several months, elevating inflationary pressure.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, currently investors are betting on a 92.30% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate-hike to be announced at the end of the two-day meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve which commenced today while the odds on rates being held at the current level stand at 7.70%.

While the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield moved higher to 5.0266%, crossing the critical 5% threshold, the 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.3858%.

On the economic front, the New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Index fell by 13 points to 7.60 in September from 20.60 of August, missing expectations of 14.75 and pointing to a moderation in manufacturing activity.

According to the Automatic Data Processing Research Institute, in the U.S., private employers added an average of 16,250 jobs per week in the four weeks ending August 29.

data.title: Caturus will nearly double export capacity of its Commonwealth LNG project
data.description:
Key points:
  • Expansion adds five liquefaction trains, lifting peak output to 17.25 million metric tons per annum
  • Caturus says it will seek customer agreements, financing and regulatory approvals in coming months
  • Facility is expected to begin exporting LNG in 2030

By Sheila Dang and Curtis Williams

U.S.-based Caturus will nearly double the export capacity of its Commonwealth LNG project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana, chief corporate affairs officer Brian Cain said on Tuesday at a G20 ministerial event in Houston.

The expansion will include five new liquefaction units, also known as trains, increasing peak output to 17.25 million metric tons per annum from the initially planned 9.5 mtpa, he said.

The project is the only fully integrated LNG venture in the U.S. that combines natural gas production with LNG processing facilities. Most U.S. LNG export projects operate as standalone infrastructure, purchasing gas from third-party producers, charging liquefaction fees and selling the superchilled gas under long-term contracts with limited exposure to spot markets.

The U.S. is the world's largest LNG exporter, and its supplies have become increasingly important in meeting global demand following disruptions to energy markets caused by Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the ongoing conflict with Iran.

"For customers worldwide, this expansion project we believe is good news because it will provide an additional source of reliable natural gas globally for decades to come," Cain said, adding that Commonwealth LNG will in the coming months focus on securing customer agreements, financing and regulatory approvals for the expansion.

Mubadala Energy, part of an Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund, holds a 24.1% stake in Caturus and participated in the project's financing. Energy investor Kimmeridge and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board also provided funding, with CPP contributing $1.2 billion and increasing its stake in Caturus to 31%.

Caturus approved construction of the LNG facility in May after securing $9.75 billion in financing for the project.

The initial development was expected to cost about $12.5 billion, including financing fees, Chairman Ben Dell said at a groundbreaking ceremony marking the project's final investment decision.

The initial phase of the project has long-term supply agreements with EQT LNG Trading, Glencore, Mercuria, Malaysia's Petronas and Saudi Aramco's trading arm.

The facility is expected to begin exporting LNG in 2030.

data.title: Ashland edges higher on report bids due this month
data.description:
Ashland ticked higher by almost 1% amid a report that the chemical maker is collecting takeover bids this month.

Apollo Global and Carlyle Group are among the financial sponsors interested in Ashland , according to traders, who cited a DealReporter article that was circulating on Tuesday.

The update comes after Bloomberg reported last month that the chemical maker was evaluating a possible sale after getting takeover interest. Advent, Apollo, and Carlyle Group () are among those that have had contact with the company.

Standard Industries Inc., which, through its investment platform Standard Investments LLC is among Ashland’s biggest shareholders, is also interested, according to the Bloomberg report.

A potential deal comes as activist investors have been pushing for months for Ashland to explore a sale. Last month, Ashland confirmed an agreement with activist investor Ancora Holdings to expand the chemical maker's board.

Ashland is set to hold its innovation day on Thursday.

data.title: PSP Investments CEO Orida Signals Interest in Canada Airports
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--The chief executive of one of Canada's biggest pension funds with experience in transport logistics abroad said she is interested in striking a deal with Ottawa to invest in the country's biggest airports.

"We're well suited for the opportunity," Deborah Orida, president and CEO of the Public Service Pension Investment Board, said in an interview Tuesday on the sidelines at an investment summit hosted by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Earlier in the day, Carney said Canada is ready to open the doors for private-sector investment in the country's four biggest airports, with cash raised to be deployed in crucial infrastructure that Canada needs.

The pension fund, also known as PSP Investments, owns seven airports, mostly in Europe, through its AviAlliance subsidiary. "We are not only an airport investor but also an airport operator," Orida said. "That makes us, I think, well positioned to participate."

PSP Investments has 320 billion Canadian dollars (US$230.2 billion) under management, and in 2025 delivered a one-year net return of 6.5% and a 10-year net annualized return of 8.8%. It is tasked with delivering returns for federal-government employees, members of the Canadian military and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

As envisaged by Carney, the airport deals would be set up as long-term concessions, which are agreements under which the private-sector investor handles the operation and maintenance of the airport for a set period. Current Canadian laws dissuade private-sector investments in airports, which are run by not-for-profit, non-share capital authorities that fund operations through fees charged to passengers and airlines.

Orida said PSP's AviAlliance has a track record that shows it can modernize airport terminals and expand route networks through its contact with airlines. The airports in the PSP portfolio include those in Athens, Glasgow and San Juan, Puerto Rico.

"We have the opportunity with our operating expertise to generate value that is not coming at the expense of the customers," Orida said. She added that the airports are a key holding in their infrastructure class, which over a five-year period has recorded average annual returns of about 15%.

According to Statistics Canada, the country's airports served 158.9 million passengers last year, with Toronto's Pearson International by far the largest, accounting for nearly 30% of passenger traffic.

The prior Liberal government administration, under former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, had an interest in encouraging more domestic investment by pension funds--drawing criticism from some pension-fund executives about any formal effort to compel asset managers to reallocate money from higher-returning opportunities.

Orida said Carney's airport announcement signals the government is looking to make good-investment opportunities more readily available for large investors like PSP. Prior to the summit, PSP unveiled plans to increase its domestic holdings by up to 40%, and cross the C$100 billion threshold in the next few years.

That pledge was driven by private-investing opportunities, "and the attractiveness of the Canadian public equities for our portfolio, rather than a government edict," she said.

Canada's largest pension fund, the CPP Investment Board, said Tuesday it would join forces with Brookfield Asset Management on a C$50 billion fund seeking opportunities in infrastructure. Prior to the summit, the five biggest Canadian banks pledged a collective C$320 billion in capital for the domestic economy.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Gnosis to Host Meetup in Lisbon on September 17th
data.description:
Gnosis will host A Fintech View on Ethereum with the Ethereum Foundation at the Lisbon Ethereum Hub at 17:30 UTC on September 17th. The event will examine Ethereum from a financial-technology perspective.

Refer to the official tweet by GNO:

Gnosis
@gnosis_

This Thursday we are back with another event at the Lisbon Ethereum Hub in collaboration with @ethereumfndn.

A Fintech View on Ethereum - topic is super timely for the whole ETH, so we expect some heated discussion.

Join us at 6:30PM Lisbon time. pic.twitter.com/kYlx5LETcH

Sep 15, 2026

GNO Info

Gnosis is a blockchain platform built on the Ethereum network that offers tools and services for creating decentralized prediction products, new models of decentralized governance, and asset management solutions.

One of Gnosis' flagship products is the Gnosis Protocol, which serves as a trading protocol providing high liquidity for any ERC20 token.

The GNO token is the native token of the Gnosis platform, utilized for participation in platform activities such as voting on governance proposals and earning rewards. GNO token holders have the option to stake their tokens to receive OWL tokens, which can be used for fee payments on the platform.
